summary_paragraph: A female patient with end-stage renal disease, systemic lupus erythematosus, antiphospholipid syndrome, and a history of hypercoagulability was admitted for acute dizziness. Evaluation revealed peripheral vestibulopathy, which resolved during the admission. She underwent a scheduled ERCP for choledocholithiasis, during which two bile duct stones were removed and a pancreatic stent was placed. Post-procedure, she developed melena from a benign-appearing ulcer at the sphincterotomy site, requiring one unit of packed red blood cells. Repeat endoscopy confirmed no active bleeding. Her liver enzymes transiently elevated but improved. Warfarin was held due to bleeding risk, with plans to restart as an outpatient. Pancytopenia was noted but stable, with workup deferred. She remained hemodynamically stable, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with follow-up for stent removal, INR monitoring, and continued dialysis.
